immune and endocrine systems. Prolactin stimulated disease in autoimmune NZB/NZW 
mice. Treatment of the mice with the prolactin-lowering dopamine agonist, 
bromocriptine, suppressed anti-DNA and prolonged life spans. These findings have 
been applied to humans with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). An open-label 
study, a double blind study, and a study comparing bromocriptine to 
hydroxychloroquine provided evidence that bromocriptine therapy reduced flares 
and suppressed disease activity in SLE.
